podcast.title: Characteristics and Lo-Fi Connection (Early 1990s)
podcast.body: Slacker Rock emerged in the early 1990s as a style of music that was laid back while maintaining a ragged-around-the-edges sound. It often overlapped with the low-fidelity aesthetic, reflecting a broader trend in alternative music following the grunge explosion. "But below that was what some people called Slacker Rock, a style that was laid back while still being ragged around the edges."
